The City of San Marino appreciates your attendance. Citizens’ interest provides the Planning
Commission with valuable information regarding issues of the community.

Regular meetings are held on the 4th Wednesday of every month at 6:00 p.m.; however, the
regular meeting of December 27, 2023, is canceled.

In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, any person with a disability who
requires a reasonable modification or accommodation in order to participate in a meeting
should contact the City via email at Planning@CityofSanMarino.org or by phone at (626) 300­
0713 prior to the meeting for assistance.

The public is welcome to attend the meeting in person or remotely via Zoom, however, the
meeting will proceed as normal even if there are technical difficulties with Zoom. The City will
do its best to resolve any technical issues as quickly as possible.

How to participate in the meeting from home:
Visit www.CityofSanMarino.org/Zoom

How to offer public comment from home:
  1. Public comment will be accepted by email to Planning@CityofSanMarino.org before or
  during the meeting prior to the close of public comment on an item, to be read during
  public comment. Lengthy public comment may be summarized in the interest of time.

  2. Public comment will be accepted electronically via the zoom.us teleconference module
  during the meeting. Zoom comments will be taken after the in­person comments.

2200 Huntington Drive, the Crowell Public Library, 1890 Huntington Drive, and the Stoneman

http://www.cityofsanmarino.org.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

The City welcomes public input. Members of the public may address the Planning Commission
by submitting a public comment request and giving it to the Community Development Director
prior to the meeting. At this time, the public may address the Planning Commission on items
that are not on the agenda. Pursuant to state law, the Planning Commission may not discuss
or take action on issues not on the meeting agenda (Government Code Section 54954.3).
 The Chair reserves the right to place limits on duration of comments. Staff may be asked to
follow up on such items.

STRATEGIC PLAN CRITICAL SUCCESS FACTORS

Attractive, Complementary Business District;
Engaged and Connected Residents;
Efficient, Responsive, and Effective City Services;
Beautiful, Preserved, Single-Family Neighborhoods

BACKGROUND

On November 21, 2023, during its special meeting, the Planning Commission
approved a proposed tenant improvement, consisting of a complete interior
remodel (CUP 23-04), and the replacement of one exterior door with a window
that matches the existing design (DR 23-96), for the existing 1,161 square-
foot Starbucks café located at 2265 Huntington Drive.

At the public hearing, the Planning Commission reviewed all of the information
provided in the staff reports and considered the testimony given at the public
hearings, including all written communications to the Planning Commission
and other pertinent information.

After the Planning Commission deliberated the merits of the project, the
Planning Commission directed staff to prepare a written Resolution of Approval
to be considered at the next available Planning Commission meeting. Please
find the attachment to the staff report, which contains the Resolution as
directed by the Planning Commission.

  PAGE 8 of 16
 RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends the Planning Commission adopt Resolution No. PCR 23-17
approving Conditional Use Permit No. CUP 23-04 and Design Review Case No.
DR 23-96.

ATTACHMENTS

1. Resolution No. PCR 23-17

   CITY OF SAN MARINO
  RESOLUTION NO. PCR 23-17

A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY OF SAN MARINO PLANNING COMMISSION
APPROVING CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT NO. CUP 23-04, REGARDING A
PROPOSED TENANT IMPROVEMENT CONSISTING OF A COMPLETE
INTERIOR REMODEL, AND DESIGN REVIEW CASE NO. DR 23-96, TO
REPLACE AN EXISTING EXTERIOR DOOR WITH A MATCHING WINDOW,
FOR THE EXISTING STARBUCKS CAFÉ LOCATED AT 2265 HUNTINGTON
DRIVE, ASSESSOR PARCEL NUMBER 5331-028-001, CITY OF SAN MARINO

  WHEREAS, on August 11, 2023, an application to consider a proposed tenant
improvement, consisting of a complete interior remodel of the existing Starbucks café, and
the replacement of one exterior door with a matching window had been duly filed by Taylor
Conterno (Applicant), for the property listed below:

  2265 Huntington Drive
  Assessor Parcel Number 5331-028-001
  San Marino, CA, 91108

  WHEREAS, the Property is Zoned C-1 General Commercial and

  WHEREAS, the property in question is legally described as follows:

  TRACT NO. 7496, THAT PORTION LYING SOUTHWEST (SW) OF THE
  NORTHEAST (NE) FORTY FEET (40’) OF LOT 1

  WHEREAS, a public hearing to consider said Conditional Use Permit applications was
set and held before the Planning Commission at its special meeting of November 21, 2023,
at the hour of 6:00 PM, and relevant testimonies, evidence and comments have been made
a part of the record; and

  WHEREAS, on November 21, 2023, the Planning Commission also reviewed all of
the information provided in the staff report and considered the testimony given at the public
hearings, including all written communications to the Planning Commission, as well as other
pertinent information; and

  WHEREAS, the proposed project is exempt from the California Environmental
Quality Act (“CEQA”) pursuant to State CEQA Guidelines, Article 19, Sections 15301 (Class
1) and 15324 (Class 24).

  NOW, THEREFORE, THE PLANNING COMMISSION OF THE CITY OF SAN
MARINO does hereby find, determine and declare:

SECTION 1. All of the above recitals are true and correct and are incorporated herein as
part of this decision by this reference.

  1  PAGE 10 of 16
 SECTION 2. The San Marino Planning Commission makes the following findings regarding
the issuance of CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT NO. CUP 23-04 for a proposed tenant
improvement consisting of a complete interior remodel of the existing Starbucks café:

  1. That the establishment, maintenance or operation of the use or building
  applied for will not, under the circumstances of the particular case, be
  detrimental to the health, safety, peace, morals, comfort or general
  welfare of persons residing in or working in the area of such proposed use
  nor be detrimental or injurious to property or improvements in the
  neighborhood or to the general welfare of the City; and

  Staff finds the proposed project will not be detrimental to the health, safety, peace, morals,
  comfort, or general welfare of persons residing in or working in the area; nor be detrimental
  or injurious to property or improvements in the neighborhood or to the general welfare of
  the City; since the proposed improvements are primarily confined to the interior. As such,
  this project meets this finding.

  2. That the site for the proposed conditional use is adequate in size and
  shape to accommodate the yards, walls and fences, parking and loading,
  landscaping and other development features prescribed in this Chapter or
  required by the Commission in order to integrate said conditional use
  with the land and uses in the neighborhood; and

  The parcel is currently improved with a 5,019 square-foot multi-tenant commercial building
  with walls, landscaping, and other development features. The structure has five tenant
  spaces. Starbucks is located within the 1,161 square-foot commercial unit located at 2265
  Huntington Drive. The proposed improvements are confined to the interior of the existing
  1,161 square-foot space, with the exception of one exterior door replacement. Staff finds
  the site is large enough to accommodate the proposed work associated with CUP 23-04.
  Therefore, this project meets this finding.

  3. That proposed conditional use will not have a detrimental effect upon the
  nature, condition and development of nearby uses and buildings; and

  Starbucks has an existing conditional use permit (CUP 94-22). Staff finds the proposed
  project is consistent with the conditions of approval listed on CUP 94-22. The existing
  conditions of approval regulate Starbucks’ use and operations in such a way that prevents
  a detrimental effect on nearby uses and buildings, including nearby residences. Additionally,
  staff finds the proposed improvements will not have a detrimental effect upon the nature,
  condition and development of nearby uses and buildings since the proposed improvements
  are primarily confined to the interior. As such, this project meets this finding.

  4. That the site for the proposed conditional use will relate to streets and
  highways adequate in width and pavement to carry the kind and quantity
  of traffic such use would generate.

  2  PAGE 11 of 16
   The site is improved with a 5,019 square-foot multi-tenant commercial building located along
  a commercial corridor and served by Huntington Drive, which is paved and adequately
  maintained. Starbucks has operated out of the commercial unit at 2265 Huntington Drive,
  which is part of the multi-tenant commercial building, for approximately 30 years. Staff finds
  the proposed improvements would not generate more traffic than the use currently
  generates. Therefore, this project meets this finding.

SECTION 3. The San Marino Planning Commission makes the following findings regarding
DESIGN REVIEW CASE NO. DR 23-96 for the replacement of one exterior door with a
matching window:
  1. That the proposed structure is compatible with the Neighborhood.

  The project involves the replacement of one door on the existing commercial structure
  located at 2265 Huntington Drive. Sheet I104 on the submitted plans demonstrates that
  the new metal window replacing the existing metal door on the north elevation will match
  the existing design. Staff finds the proposed change will maintain the compatibility with the
  other units on found on the multi-tenant commercial structure, and generally with other
  commercial buildings in the Neighborhood. Staff also recommends a condition to ensure the
  window material, color, texture, and design will match seamlessly with the existing building
  help this project meet this finding. As such, this project meets this finding.

  2. That the proposed structure is designed and will be developed in a manner
  which balances the reasonable expectation of privacy of persons residing
  on contiguous properties with the reasonable expectations of the
  applicants to develop their property within the restrictions of this code.

  The project proposes no changes in which this finding applies.

  3. In the case of a building addition, the proposal is compatible with the
  existing building which includes the rooflines.

  The project proposes no changes in which this finding applies.

  4. That the colors and materials are consistent and match the existing
  building or structure.

  The proposed project involves the replacement of one exterior door with a window that
  matches the existing window design. Sheet I104 on the submitted plans shows the proposed
  floor finish plan and north elevation. Keynote 13 on Sheet I104 states that the proposed
  storefront window mullions will match the existing width and color; and that the glass tint
  will match the existing window, as well. Staff recommends a condition to ensure the window
  material, color, texture, and design will match seamlessly with the existing building help this
  project meet this finding. Therefore, this project meets this finding.

  3  PAGE 12 of 16
 SECTION 4. PURSUANT TO THE ABOVE FINDINGS, IT IS RESOLVED that the San
Marino Planning Commission hereby approves CUP 23-04 & DR 23-96, each subject to the
conditions of approval which are attached hereto and incorporated herein by this reference.

SECTION 5. The project is exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act
(“CEQA”) pursuant to State CEQA Guidelines, Article 19, Sections 15301 (Class 1, Existing
Facilities), and there is no substantial evidence demonstrating that an exception to a
categorical exemption pursuant to CEQA Guidelines, Section 15300.2 applies.

SECTION 6. The decision of the Planning Commission, as set forth in this Resolution, is
final unless a timely appeal to the City Council is filed within fifteen (15) days of the date of
the adoption of this Resolution by the Planning Commission pursuant to the provisions of
Section 23.07.09 of the San Marino Municipal Code.

  VOTE:  AYES:  WRIGHT, BRODY, CHENG
  NOES:  DUSTIN, BOYLE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE
